question: Which conditional distributions in the training data shape token embedding and unembedding geometry, and can those distributional 'probability signatures' explain ordered synthetic representations and similarity blocks learned by small language models?

key_findings.claim: The paper defines four probability signatures that expose label association, token co-occurrence, label-conditioned co-occurrence, and reverse input-given-label structure, then places them explicitly in embedding and unembedding gradient-flow equations.
key_findings.evidence: For an embedding-based model, Propositions 1-2 group per-example gradients by token and label counts. The four signatures are phi_y|x, phi_X|x, phi_X|y,x, and phi_X|y. They are ordinary empirical conditional distributions arranged as vectors or matrices, allowing the later small-initialization expansions to identify which data term enters at which order.

key_findings.claim: Three controlled composite-addition datasets isolate different signatures while preserving the same ordered anchor tokens, providing a designed test of which distribution can induce ordered geometry.
key_findings.evidence: Ordinary addition changes label-given-anchor while holding anchor co-occurrence fixed; same-output-domain addition changes input co-occurrence while holding label-given-anchor fixed; modular addition holds both of those fixed but changes label-conditioned co-occurrence. Linear models fit the first two tasks, while the modular task requires the feedforward nonlinearity.

key_findings.claim: The ordered anchor-embedding geometry follows different signature terms in the three synthetic tasks, including a predicted difference in formation speed.
key_findings.evidence: In the linear model, ordinary addition develops ordered anchor cosine structure through the leading label-distribution term, whereas same-output-domain addition develops it more slowly through a co-occurrence term multiplied by small embedding/unembedding matrices. Modular addition collapses linear-model anchors toward one direction because both signatures match across anchors, but a feedforward model recovers order through the label-conditioned co-occurrence term.

key_findings.claim: Unembedding vectors acquire label order that is associated with the reverse input-given-label signature, including a ring for modular addition.
key_findings.evidence: Across all three tasks, label-token unembedding cosines and PCA projections form sequence-aligned structures. Corollary 3 makes the reverse conditional distribution phi_X|label the leading data-dependent term; the modular label wrap-around corresponds to a ring in unembedding space, and the feedforward appendix reproduces ordered unembeddings.

key_findings.claim: In small decoder-only language models trained from scratch, next-token and previous-token conditional distributions align most strongly with high-similarity blocks in embedding and unembedding space.
key_findings.evidence: Twelve-layer, width-512 Qwen2.5 models are trained for one epoch on each of five Pile subsets. Heatmaps, tokenwise correlation plots, and percentile-conditioned comparisons show that next-token signatures track embedding cosine and previous-token signatures track unembedding cosine, with much stronger agreement in the highest embedding-similarity percentiles. A denominator-token case study links shared contexts such as '*' and ')' to one high-similarity block.

key_findings.claim: The empirical LLM relationship transfers to a Llama-2 architecture and can approximately recover prominent blocks and digit order in a tied-embedding Qwen2.5-3B base model, but the paper explicitly limits that estimator to favorable initialization and corpus match.
key_findings.evidence: Repeating the Pile-subset training with Llama-2 preserves the qualitative correlation and high-percentile agreement. For tied Qwen2.5-3B embeddings, adding next- and previous-token signatures estimated from the five public subsets recovers visible high-similarity subblocks and digit order; the authors warn that unknown pretraining data and initialization can prevent generalization to other base models.

key_findings.claim: The theoretical bridge is a local small-initialization approximation, not an exact causal model of full transformer training.
key_findings.evidence: The corollary proofs expand softmax around small logits, approximate the feedforward activation by a low-order polynomial, take the infinite-data limit, and place output-probability, residual-transformer, and higher-order contributions into eta remainders. The conclusion names self-attention and a comprehensive theory as future work.

method.core_idea: Express embedding updates in a basis of empirical conditional token distributions, then manipulate those distributions in controlled datasets to see which one predicts the learned cosine geometry.
method.mechanism: Per-example cross-entropy gradients are grouped by whether a token occurs and which label or adjacent token follows it. In a linear model, a small-logit softmax expansion makes label-given-token the leading embedding term and token co-occurrence a higher-order term; in a ReLU feedforward model, a polynomial approximation introduces label-conditioned co-occurrence. A parallel derivation makes input-given-label lead unembedding updates. For autoregressive models, the same grouping yields next-token and previous-token signatures plus unresolved output-probability and residual-network terms. The paper compares pairwise cosine matrices, PCA projections, an anchor-order statistic, tokenwise correlations, and percentile ranks between signatures and learned parameters.
assumptions: Training samples converge to a fixed population distribution as N approaches infinity.
Initialization and logits remain small enough for low-order softmax and parameter expansions to dominate the reviewed training interval.
The feedforward activation can be represented adequately by the chosen low-order polynomial locally, despite the experimental use of ReLU.
Remainder terms containing model output probabilities, higher orders, and the transformer's residual computation do not overturn the displayed leading signature relationship.
Cosine similarity between conditional-distribution vectors is an appropriate proxy for semantic relationship.
The deliberately uniform synthetic tasks isolate one signature without introducing an unmeasured alternative explanation.
Five Pile subsets approximate the relevant adjacent-token distribution well enough for the tested small models and for the Qwen2.5-3B case study.

techniques.role: Encodes label, co-occurrence, label-conditioned co-occurrence, and reverse-label associations as comparable vectors.
Rewrites embedding and unembedding dynamics by token/label occurrence classes before approximation.
Constructs three datasets where different conditional distributions vary across ordered anchor tokens.
Ranks data-dependent terms by order in the embedding and unembedding matrices.
Compares the full token-token similarity matrices of signatures and learned parameters.
Tests whether distributional similarity is disproportionately accurate for the model's strongest embedding pairs.
Adds next- and previous-token signatures when one parameter matrix serves both input and output roles.

evaluations.setting: Three 50,000-example composite-addition datasets with anchors 11-20, keys/labels 101-140, a width-200 linear model and width-200 one-hidden-layer ReLU network, AdamW, batch size 100, and 1,000 epochs.
evaluations.metric: Training accuracy and whether anchor embedding cosine/PCA geometry respects numerical anchor distance over training.
evaluations.result: The linear model fits ordinary and same-output-domain addition but not modular addition; both fitted tasks develop ordered anchor geometry, while modular anchors align in the linear model and become ordered only in the nonlinear model.
evaluations.baseline: The same architecture across datasets engineered to hold different signatures constant.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic embedding and unembedding dynamics under the three task distributions.
evaluations.metric: Cosine matrices, PCA projections, the R_order statistic, and qualitative agreement with gradient-flow corollaries.
evaluations.result: Signature and parameter geometries show matching hierarchy or ring structure, and the same-output-domain hierarchy emerges later as predicted by its higher-order term; scalar effect sizes, seed variation, and confidence intervals are not reported.
evaluations.baseline: Random initialization, alternate task signatures, and linear versus feedforward architectures.

evaluations.setting: Five 12-layer, 12-head, width-512 Qwen2.5 models trained for one epoch separately on Pile-ArXiv, DM Mathematics, Common Crawl, PubMed Central, and Wikipedia, sequence length 2,048.
evaluations.metric: Correlation between embedding and signature cosine rows for the 10,000 most frequent tokens per subset, plus signature percentile conditional on embedding-similarity decile.
evaluations.result: The paper reports positive tokenwise alignment and much stronger correspondence for high-similarity embedding pairs; the PDF figures carry the quantitative curves but the prose does not report aggregate coefficients or uncertainty.
evaluations.baseline: Low- and middle-similarity percentile bins and the independently trained models across five domains.

evaluations.setting: One matched Llama-2 architecture experiment on the same Pile subsets and training configuration.
evaluations.metric: The same embedding/signature heatmaps, row correlations, and percentile-conditioned summaries.
evaluations.result: Qualitative relationships closely track the Qwen2.5 results, especially for high-similarity regions.

evaluations.setting: Pretrained tied-embedding Qwen2.5-3B base analyzed using a signature estimated from the union of the five public subsets.
evaluations.metric: Cosine-similarity subblocks for frequent tokens and digits 0-9.
evaluations.result: The estimated signature recovers prominent high-similarity blocks and an ordered digit pattern visually, with an explicit warning that the result depends on unknown true pretraining data and initialization.
evaluations.baseline: The model's learned tied-embedding cosine matrix.

evaluations.setting: DM Mathematics denominator-like tokens '/a', '/b', '/c', '/d', and absent '/e'.
evaluations.metric: Embedding cosine, signature cosine, and sampled following contexts.
evaluations.result: Observed tokens share high similarity and common next tokens such as '*' and ')'; the unseen '/e' breaks the pattern.
evaluations.baseline: A spelling-matched token absent from the training subset.

limitations: Author-stated: the present LLM derivation does not incorporate self-attention explicitly; subtle relationships are left to future theory.

Author-stated: estimating a base model's tied-embedding geometry from public text is sensitive to the model's initialization and unknown true training corpus and may not generalize across open models.

Reviewer inference: the synthetic tasks are engineered so one named conditional distribution carries the anchor order, making them a mechanism demonstration rather than evidence that natural-language semantics are generally generated this way.

Reviewer inference: the transformer corollary leaves output-probability, residual-network, and higher-order terms in eta; the realistic experiments therefore show correlation, not that the displayed signature is the dominant causal gradient component.
Reviewer inference: the models called LLMs in the controlled experiment are small width-512 decoders trained for only one epoch, not pretrained models at contemporary large scale.
Reviewer inference: no counterfactual corpus reweighting holds token meaning fixed while selectively changing a signature, so natural-corpus causal identification is absent.
Reviewer inference: the paper reports no repeated seeds, error bars, sampling uncertainty, or quantitative table for its principal Qwen/Llama alignment figures.
Reviewer inference: restricting analysis to each subset's 10,000 most frequent tokens favors dense conditional-distribution estimates and leaves rare-token geometry untested.

Reviewer inference: the signature terminology repackages conditional distributions and co-occurrence matrices whose relation to static embedding geometry has substantial prior theory; novelty lies in the dynamic multi-signature application, not the existence of distribution-geometry links.
failure_modes: Two tokens can share next-token distributions but differ through long-range context, attention routing, morphology, or role, causing the signature to merge distinct representations.
Sparse or rare tokens yield noisy conditional vectors and unstable cosines, particularly outside the frequent-token panel.
Later training can make output-probability and nonlinear residual terms comparable to or larger than the small-initialization leading term.
Changing a corpus signature usually changes many other statistics simultaneously, so an apparent causal effect can be due to sequence length, frequency, label support, or optimization exposure.
Weight tying adds input and output gradients; using only a next-token signature or only a previous-token signature can mispredict the combined geometry.
Tokenization changes which units have a coherent semantic interpretation and can turn shared orthographic contexts into high similarity without shared meaning.
Cosine-matrix correlation can be driven by a few large blocks or token-frequency strata and need not predict individual pair geometry.
An estimated public-corpus signature can look correct on selected digit or frequent-token blocks while failing globally because the true pretraining mixture is unknown.
reusable_insights: Rewrite parameter gradients by empirical event classes before inventing a representation-level explanation; the coefficients often reveal which corpus statistics can matter at leading order.
Use controlled distributions that swap which statistic varies while keeping labels, vocabulary, architecture, and optimizer fixed.
Distinguish embedding-side and unembedding-side data statistics, especially when parameters are untied.
With tied embeddings, combine both temporal directions rather than treating the matrix as only an input lookup table.
Analyze high-similarity and low-similarity pairs separately; an aggregate correlation can hide where a signature is informative.
Include an absent or deliberately decorrelated token in qualitative cases to expose simple orthographic or frequency explanations.
State the approximation regime alongside any gradient-flow mechanism and measure when neglected terms become large.
open_questions: Can corpus reweighting or synthetic text interventions selectively change next-token similarity while preserving token frequency and higher-order semantics, yielding a causal geometry test?
How much additional embedding structure is explained by attention-conditioned, position-conditioned, or longer-context probability signatures beyond adjacent tokens?
Do the signature relationships persist through full multi-epoch pretraining, scale, normalization, and realistic optimizer schedules?
Can signature estimates predict geometry before training, including confidence intervals for rare tokens and held-out domains?
Which remainder terms in the transformer derivation dominate after the small-initialization phase, and can they be measured directly from checkpoints?
Does altering probability-signature geometry improve reasoning or transfer, or merely rotate parameters without behavioral benefit?
Can one separate semantic co-occurrence from tokenizer, syntax, and absolute-position effects using matched corpora?
How do probability signatures relate to local activation regions and intrinsic dimension beyond the input/output embedding matrices?

competitive_landscape.title: Isotropy in the Contextual Embedding Space: Clusters and Manifolds
competitive_landscape.difference: Cai et al. diagnose clusters, centered within-cluster cosine, frequency/position structure, and local intrinsic dimension in pretrained contextual activations. Probability Signature instead targets learned input/output parameter geometry and derives conditional-distribution gradient terms, but its natural-language evidence is narrower and correlational.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2021 OpenReview record; audited original-ID PDF inspected

competitive_landscape.title: How Contextual are Contextualized Word Representations? Comparing the Geometry of BERT, ELMo, and GPT-2 Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Ethayarajh quantifies anisotropy, context specificity, and the small variance explained by static word identity across pretrained layers. This paper asks what data distribution creates parameter-level similarities and adds controlled training dynamics rather than describing contextual activation geometry alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Representation Degeneration Problem in Training Natural Language Generation Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Gao et al. analyze how likelihood training with weight tying produces a narrow cone and propose a cosine regularizer with language-modeling and translation gains. Probability Signature models pair-specific organization from conditional data distributions and does not propose an isotropy regularizer or downstream improvement.

competitive_landscape.title: Analyzing Transformers in Embedding Space
competitive_landscape.difference: Dar et al. project trained transformer parameters into vocabulary space for zero-pass interpretation, model alignment, and classifier translation. This paper instead explains how selected embedding/unembedding similarities arise during training from data-conditionals and does not interpret every transformer block.

competitive_landscape.title: Initialization is Critical to Whether Transformers Fit Composite Functions by Reasoning or Memorizing
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. show initialization scale selects inferential versus memorizing solutions and analyzes their information flow and vector structures. Probability Signature keeps small initialization fixed and varies conditional data distributions to attribute which statistic organizes anchors; it does not compare solution generalization regimes.

competitive_landscape.title: Reasoning Bias of Next Token Prediction Training
competitive_landscape.difference: Yao et al. compare next-token and critical-token objectives and attribute NTP's reasoning advantage to noise-induced regularization, validated on reasoning tasks and perturbations. Probability Signature derives adjacent-token conditional geometry under NTP but supplies no matched reasoning-performance test.

competitive_landscape.title: A Latent Variable Model Approach to PMI-based Word Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Arora et al. derive co-occurrence statistics and linear analogy structure from a latent discourse model for static embeddings, providing a theoretical account of PMI, word2vec, and GloVe. Probability Signature treats several conditional distributions dynamically in supervised and autoregressive neural training rather than positing a static generative discourse model.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Word Embedding as Implicit Matrix Factorization
competitive_landscape.difference: Levy and Goldberg prove that SGNS implicitly factorizes shifted PMI and compare explicit SVD/PPMI solutions on similarity and analogy tasks. Probability Signature generalizes beyond one static co-occurrence matrix to embedding and unembedding gradient dynamics, nonlinear synthetic tasks, and adjacent-token distributions in decoders, but does not offer the same optimum-level equivalence.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 2014 proceedings abstract and paper record inspected 2026-08-23

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors present probability signatures as a novel bridge explaining how semantic relationships in the data form embedding structures through optimization dynamics.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Static co-occurrence/PMI theory, anisotropy analyses, embedding-space parameter interpretation, and initialization-dependent composite-task representations all predate the work. The new combination is a taxonomy of conditional distributions placed in embedding and unembedding gradient flow, signature-isolating addition tasks, and a high-similarity alignment test in trained decoders.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The synthetic mechanism decomposition is distinctive and reusable. The broad claim that data semantics causally determine realistic LLM embedding structure should be narrowed: current decoder results establish pairwise association under small from-scratch models, while attention, later training, unknown corpus mixture, and direct counterfactual interventions remain unresolved.

reviewer_notes: All 23 extracted pages were inspected, including exact task distributions, tied-embedding derivation, complete Pile panels, denominator case, Llama-2 replication, and all gradient proofs.
